schema_description: Living Hearing Profile — sovereign, user-owned, versioned hearing data. Extends openhear-audiogram-v1 with preference, context, haptic and history layers.
subject: Lewis Burgess

clinical_core.comment: Immutable clinical measurements. Append only via history layer; never mutate in place.
clinical_core.source: Dorothy Thomson Hearing Services, 12 Southend Ave, Darlington, DL3 7HL
clinical_core.notes: Most recent verified clinical audiogram. ISQ (no significant change) from prior tests dating back to 2017-01-19. High-frequency sloping sensorineural loss — the public reference profile for OpenHear.

preference_layer.comment: User-defined loudness and comfort preferences. Evolves over time. Refined with lived-experience signals through 2026-08-25.

loudness_growth.comment: Per-frequency gain offset applied on top of clinical prescription. Positive = louder, negative = quieter. Mid-frequency lift prioritised for speech intelligibility under high-frequency sloping loss.

preference_layer.notes: Mid-band lift for speech clarity under sloping loss. Sustained listening effort leads to switching-off. Loudness intolerance / recruitment: amplified sound can become the problem — people remove aids or change programmes even when residual environmental awareness remains. Lived-experience signal (2026-08-25): deliberate aid-out recovery time (first thing in the morning and before sleep) is a common self-management strategy; the profile and any haptic path must respect intentional quiet periods rather than treating aid-out as non-compliance. Poorly matched amplification and dual-earpiece / stereo content can trigger or worsen tinnitus — preference and media contexts should allow mono / single-sided friendly behaviour. When an Auracast clean feed is active, preference offsets still apply; aggressive room-noise strategies should step down.

context_map.comment: Situational listening presets. Expanded through 2026-08-25 with SSD spatial awareness, multi-talker processing lag, hard acoustic environments, and institutional pathway failure signals. See also docs/AURACAST.md and docs/HEARING_LOSS_AND_DEMENTIA.md.

contexts.name: quiet_conversation
contexts.label: Quiet room, one-to-one conversation
contexts.notes: Often the only setting where current aids feel helpful, especially face-to-face with lip-reading support.

contexts.name: familiar_speaker
contexts.label: Known / familiar talker (e.g. partner or regular voice)
contexts.notes: Familiar voices remain markedly easier than novel accents or unexpected conversational shifts.

contexts.name: noisy_environment
contexts.label: Pub, restaurant, crowded social space, school / hard-surface room
contexts.notes: Persistent failure mode. Multi-talker scenes, background music, and strong accents: speech is present but not intelligible. Hard acoustic environments (high ceilings, tiled corridors, classrooms) amplify the problem; environmental modification (e.g. carpet) can matter as much as device settings. Loudness intolerance and social withdrawal over time. Primary target for effort reduction and complementary haptic support.

contexts.name: clinical_environment
contexts.label: Hospital ward / ICU / medical appointment — alarms + concurrent speech
contexts.notes: Alarms mask concurrent speech. Appointments remain difficult without quiet space or professional adjustment.

contexts.name: music
contexts.label: Music listening (headphones or speakers)
contexts.notes: Stereo content can drop dialogue or instruments on the non-hearing side for SSD users; dual-earpiece headphones may trigger tinnitus. Prefer mono-friendly or single-sided routing where the profile indicates asymmetric loss.

contexts.name: outdoors
contexts.label: Outdoors — wind, traffic, open space
contexts.notes: Lived-experience signal (SSD): reduced spatial awareness — sound from the deaf side and from behind is harder to locate; people compensate with vision near roads and cycle paths. Haptic directional or traffic cues can support safety without adding more amplified noise.

contexts.name: phone_call
contexts.label: Telephone / video call / multi-person meeting
contexts.notes: Streaming can work for expected strands; drops when topic shifts or multiple people speak. Lived-experience signal: processing lag — the listener works a beat behind, combining residual audio, lip-reading, and context; turn-taking is easily misjudged (uncomfortable pauses or accidental interruption). Group meetings are a common failure mode; email follow-up is sometimes the only workable alternative.

contexts.name: transport
contexts.label: Public transport — announcements and carriage noise
contexts.notes: Platform and carriage announcements are often unusable; people rely on visual boards. Auracast deployment in transport is a high-value complement when the user’s aid supports it.

contexts.name: auracast_venue
contexts.label: Auracast / LE Audio broadcast — clean feed in a public space
contexts.notes: Clean source (announcement, stage, TV, language track). Prefer preference-layer shaping over aggressive room-noise strategies. Continuous stream speech should not drive continuous haptic voice pulses. Chicken-and-egg: aids are increasingly Auracast-compatible; venue and transport deployment lag. See docs/AURACAST.md.

haptic_layer.comment: Haptic substitution weights. Role includes non-surgical bridge when speech-in-noise fails, when loudness is intolerable, and when spatial awareness is reduced (e.g. SSD). When an Auracast clean feed is active, continuous stream speech should not generate continuous voice haptics.

sound_classes.name: voice
sound_classes.note: Speech priority. Short onset cues in multi-talker overload can reduce the effort of catching the next word. Do not continuous-pulse on a clean Auracast stream.

sound_classes.name: alarm
sound_classes.note: Safety critical. Prefer haptic in clinical_environment.

sound_classes.name: infant_cry
sound_classes.note: High urgency for parent and clinical environments.

sound_classes.name: doorbell
sound_classes.note: Strong substitution where high-frequency loss is severe.

sound_classes.name: traffic
sound_classes.note: Safety-relevant outdoors, especially where SSD reduces spatial awareness of vehicles approaching from the deaf side or from behind.

sound_classes.name: media
sound_classes.note: User can raise; respect tinnitus and mono/single-sided preferences.

sound_classes.name: silence
sound_classes.note: No haptic for silence. Respect intentional aid-out recovery periods.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Incorporated detailed RNID-panel lived experience (sudden-onset single-sided deafness, long NHS-then-private pathway): (1) spatial awareness loss — ‘bubble’, reduced rear/deaf-side localisation, visual compensation near roads; (2) conversation processing lag and turn-taking misjudgement in multi-person meetings; (3) tinnitus triggered by unmatched amplification and dual-earpiece/stereo content — mono/single-sided friendly media behaviour; (4) deliberate aid-out recovery time (morning / before sleep) as legitimate self-management, not non-compliance; (5) hard acoustic environments (schools, tiled corridors) where environmental modification matters; (6) institutional pattern of full needs review then ignore — reinforces citizen-owned Living Hearing Profile as the record that cannot be discarded between appointments; (7) Auracast chicken-and-egg and unusable platform announcements reinforced in transport and auracast_venue notes. Preference, context, and haptic layers updated.
